title: Treasury Secretary Bessent Rejects Systemic Risks from AI Boom
summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent believes the current expansion of artificial intelligence does not pose a danger to the broader financial system. Speaking at a closed-door conference, Bessent dismissed comparisons to the dotcom bubble and argued that the founders of the industry's most profitable companies have 99% of their net worth invested in their own firms.

The remarks were made during an interview with Bridgewater CEO Nir Bar Dea and witnessed by hundreds of investors, according to the Financial Times. Bessent asserted he is adept at identifying issues within systems and sees no such systemic problem emerging from the AI sector.

selectedTweets.text:
FT: Treasury secretary Scott Bessent told investors in a private meeting that he did not see a “systemic problem” with the AI boom, downplaying concerns that the industry is in a bubble like the one that preceded the dotcom bust.

“I’m good at figuring out when there are problems in systems,” Bessent, said when asked about AI in an interview with Bridgewater chief executive Nir Bar Dea, according to three people who were present at the event. “I don’t see a systemic problem.”
